The longer I follow this topic, the stranger it becomes. Let’s assume for a moment that Bambu is right and the printer is working as designed.

After review we have confirmed that the sound you described is the normal printing sound produced when the toolhead repeatedly starts and stops rapidly while printing small models. Please rest assured that you can continue using the printer.

Then what is actually left to discuss?

That a printer makes noise? That users would prefer a quieter printer? As I said, under the assumption that the machine is not defective, the conversation seems to shift away from reliability or quality issues and more toward expectations and personal tolerance for noise.

My guess is that this is simply a story of a bad lemon.

Considering how many units have been sold by now (H3 & H2) - there have only been a handful of confirmed cases on the forum: one related to the HC - this one - and maybe two or three related to the H2. I’m not counting the obvious throwaway or fake accounts that only posted a one-line comment and never followed up.

If this were a widespread firmware or manufacturing issue, the forum would likely be flooded with complaints. Not to defend Bambu, but that’s usually how these things go. If a problem is genuinely widespread, the forum tends to get flooded with reports and complaints very quickly.
items.translation: 这帖越看越奇怪。假设拓竹是对的、机器确实按设计工作——「经复核，您描述的声音是打印小模型时工具头反复快速启停产生的正常打印声，请放心继续使用」——那还剩什么可讨论的？打印机有声音？用户希望更安静？也就是说，在「机器没有缺陷」这个假设下，话题就从可靠性/质量问题，滑向了预期管理和个人对噪音的容忍度。我猜这大概就是买了一台次品（lemon）的故事。考虑到 H3 和 H2 已经卖出这么多台，出问题的只是少数……

I think that @Sebo3D1 did a pretty good article in the Announcement section on the H3C, asking what the user does with their 3D printer.

So I would love to know just who the Target Consumer for the P3C and the H3C is going to be. I think that that is the thing that is going to influence what is going to be on the new P3C that is different from the H3C.

I am new to 3D printing, but selected the P2S, mainly from reviews and reading this forum which is a massive help. I am an average Joe, am not a print farmer, have no real interest in printing with Engineering filaments, but am eventually going to print with TPU, and maybe ABS. But at the moment it is all PLA, and PETG. BUT I am also wanting to print in multicolour. So for me I can’t really justify the extra cost of a H3C, and hope the P3C is all that I want it to be.

So, for new users, and for the average person wanting to get into 3D printing, and wanting to print multi-colours out of the box relatively quickly will the P3C be a marketing coup for BambuLabs, and what will set it apart from others. Also, for us average users will it be worth upgrading, or best to just stick with the P2S?

Potential Pros

7 Nozzles - Utilising the CMYKW colour system for multi-colours.
Multiple different nozzle sizes and ability to use on same model
Faster print speed
Less poop waste due to more nozzles
Easier access to parts that need maintai

Printer: Bambu Lab H3C
Problem
The H3C still uses a prime tower , takes up build plate space, and increases print time. and its waste anyways!

Hotend A continues printing normally.

Hotend B is already preheating in preparation for the next toolchange.

Shortly before the toolchange, Hotend B performs a small purge into a dedicated waste bucket below its parking position.

The printer switches to Hotend B and immediately continues printing without visiting a prime tower.

The lower dampers/covers beneath the parked hotends could potentially be redesigned or removed to create an open path for purged filament.

A small removable poop bucket could be installed underneath.

More usable build plate space

If an H2C/A2L build plate is reused on the H3C, the gap between its leading edge and the SwapTek Rack is only about 2 mm after installation. Due to dimensional chain tolerances and user placement deviations, there is a risk of collision or scraping between the PrintTool and the build plate. items.originalText:
H3C Arrives Less Than a Year After H2C — What About Existing Flagship Owners? We Need an FTS 2.0.
As an H2C owner who has invested heavily in Bambu Lab’s ecosystem, I have mixed feelings about the H3C announcement.

The H2C was officially unveiled in November 2025. Less than a year later, Bambu Lab has introduced the H3C, featuring an entirely new tool-changing architecture.

Technological progress is welcome. I don’t expect Bambu Lab to stop developing new products.

But I do expect a company to fully support its existing flagship products before shifting the spotlight to the next generation.

The H2C remains excellent hardware, yet some of its potential is still locked behind software limitations and poorly integrated accessories.
1. The Filament Track Switch Is Too Limited
I currently use four AMS 2 Pro units and two AMS HT units with my H2C.

The current Filament Track Switch (FTS) has only two inputs. In my setup, two AMS units share one input, while the other four share the second input through filament adapters.

As a result, switching between filaments from AMS units sharing the same input still requires retracting the previous filament through the shared path.

This significantly reduces the potential time-saving benefits of the FTS.

In many situations, the FTS mainly provides the convenience of routing filaments to either nozzle rather than a substantial improvement

items.originalText:
I remember last year when the H2C was announced (early due to the U1) and bragging that they had looked at tool changers and determined that technology to be unsuitable for 3D printing, instead going for an entirely different ‘solution’.

It turned out the Snapmaker U1 was an excellent printer at an ever improving price point, using tool changers.

A year goes by and suddenly amnesia sets in and tool changers are the only way forward, who knew, me and many others here who called it.

So, the H2C is dead technology with those who bought it going to suffer hard to source parts.

Abandonware - H2C, yes it will be sold for a while as they get rid of stock.

The H3C is an expensive solution without much new stuff. Many headed tool changers exist, the swap speed is average, the support for multiple nozzle sizes has been done for a couple of years by others (and promised by BL over 18 months ago).

It is disappointing that a company who set out to make 3D printing available to the masses is increasing the base price of the flagship each time they launch one. Cheaper than the most expensive competitors (just), but far more expensive than the direction of the market.

The H3C is almost 3 times more expensive than the very first printer they launched, the X1.

Does this look like a good printer, yes, does this look like it is worth the price, absolutely not.
items.translation: 我记得去年 H2C 发布的时候（因为 U1 而提前），还大肆宣传……（下略，原文 1370 字，完整复盘 H2C 到 H3C 的发布节奏）

items.originalText:
illien:

Difference here, specifically the unloading, is in the 1st/2nd gen implementation, you don’t need to do anything to complete unloading. manual pull back here sounds to me like what the machine asks you to do for external filaments - if not, the task is not completed.

It’s a manual unload, regardless.

The purge is nearly 0! it’s awesome. The filaments are always loaded in the toolheads though, until you go into the UI and unload them. When you unload the filament, it’ll pick the tool head up, cut the filament, then prompt you to pull it out.

The loading process for the regular AMS slots is mostly automatic though. You put the spool in, put the filament into the tube, and it’ll pull it in. However, you still have to go into the UI and load the filament into the tool head.

TPU, you manually plug into the tool head. External is the same, surely. I imagine an external AMS unit though would probably auto-rewind it though, like it does on the other printers.
items.translation: 这里的区别，具体是退料环节，在于第一/第二代的实现方式：你不需要做任何动作就完成了退料。而这里的手动回抽，听起来像是机器对外部料路的做法——如果不拔，任务就没完成。无论如何，这是手动退料。但冲刷量几乎是零！这很棒。耗材会一直留在工具头里，直到你进 UI 卸载它。当你卸载时，它会抬起工具头、切断耗材，然后提示你把它拔出来。普通 AMS 槽位的进料过程基本是自动的：你把料盘放进去、把耗材塞进管子里，它就会自己拉进去。但你还是得进 UI 把耗材加载到工具头。TPU 则要手动插到工具头上。
items.summaryCn: 论坛里对 AMS 3H 装卸料流程描述得最完整的一条，且给出关键实测：换色冲刷量几乎为零（原文 the purge is nearly 0! it's awesome）。流程是——耗材常驻工具头，UI 触发退料后机器抬头、切料、提示手动拔出；普通 AMS 槽位进料半自动，末端仍需在 UI 里确认送入工具头。这条把"手动退料"从缺点重新定位成流程设计：废料接近零本身就是这个取舍换来的。

I mean with the rumored price of about $3000 what exactly is the target audience for that machine?

People printing technical filaments are on the H2S or H2D and people using their printers for multi colour prints are on the P2S, X2D or at best the H2C.

This audience surely won’t drop $3000 onto something just to print their pokemon figures faster.

I’m on the H2S right now and thought about switching, but with that price tag, no thanks.

user_1843457038:

Software is where improvements lie for a 3d printer after launch. Hardware improvements will primarily be rolling changes to optimize costs and warranty claims. I am directly referring to software.

Who says that the software improvements for the H2D or H2C will stop at the launch of the H3C?

And why wouldn’t they be allowed to launch a new machine before they fully implemented all the promised features in the older one?

Multi-size nozzle printing is something that all 3D printer vendors have quite high on their list as it is a serious differentiator.

And yes, that is software. We currently have no idea if the new slicer wil also support multi-layer heights or just only multi-size nozzles.

And I am 100% sure that the release will definitely not be mature in that aspect.

If you look at how long it took before we matured FDM printing, from the first NC glue gun to what the 3D printers are now.

Those developments run in parallel and the hardware doesn’t have to wait for the software to mature or vice versa.

If that would be the case, improvements in technology would take ages.

Yes, it feels bad to some, that when they bought the best of the best at a certain time, and just hear weeks after that the same company or a competitor came out with something better.

items.translation: 我说的是软件。3D 打印机发布后的改进主要在软件，硬件改动基本是优化成本和保修的滚动变更。谁说 H2D/H2C 的软件改进会因为 H3C 发布就停止？为什么不能在旧机型承诺功能全部落地前发新机？多口径喷嘴打印是所有厂商都排得很高的差异化点，而且那是软件能力。我们目前完全不知道新切片器会不会支持多层高，还是只支持多口径喷嘴。我百分之百确定这一块首发时肯定不成熟，看看以往功能成熟花了多久就知道。
